title: Delayed Histiocytic Foreign Body Reaction and Granuloma Formation Following Argiform Injection for Soft Tissue Augmentation Mimicking a Lipomatous Tumor on Histopathology: A Case Report.
abstract: As cosmetic procedures gain popularity, the use of nonapproved soft-tissue fillers by unlicensed or untrained practitioners in nonmedical settings is rising. We report a rare case of a histiocytic reaction to foreign material following Argiform injection. A 31-year-old female presented with a 2 year history of an itchy and painful rash on both buttocks. The rash was initially confined to the right buttock but extended to the left several months later; it remained refractory to topical ointments. A skin punch biopsy revealed extensive adipocytic-like cells within the dermis, some of which mimicked lipoblasts. Immunohistochemistry showed the lesional cells were positive for CD68 and negative for S100 and pancytokeratin. A final diagnosis of a histiocytic reaction to foreign material was made. Following the biopsy results, the patient disclosed a history of cosmetic Argiform injections at a spa 4-5 years prior to presentation. This case demonstrates that delayed tissue reactions to Argiform can mimic lipomatous tumors, creating a significant diagnostic pitfall. Clinicopathologic correlation, including a thorough remote medical history, is critical for achieving an accurate diagnosis.

title: The risk of radiotherapy toxicity in patients with laryngeal cancer: predictive factors and radiobiological modelling.
abstract: Introduction The assessment of post-radiation toxicity and quality of life is a crucial aspect of patient care. To evaluate and predict post-irradiation toxicity in a cohort of patients with laryngeal cancer, radiobiological modelling, biological and medical indicators, dose-volume variables, and radiomics were used. Methods For the comprehensive evaluation, biological and medical factors, treatment plan doses, and radiomic features from pre-treatment CT images were analyzed using the PyRadiomics Python library. The Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) and Niemierko general equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) formalisms were applied for modelling and parameter estimation. The chi-square test assessed significance between categorical variables, while one-way ANOVA and the Spearman correlation were applied for continuous variables. All analyses were conducted using a custom Python 3.8 script. Results Significant indicators impacting post-irradiation toxicity were identified. The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) comorbidity score, pre-treatment body weight loss, and weight loss during therapy were consistently associated with acute hematological, skin, and gastrointestinal toxicities. For late outcomes, pre-treatment weight loss, alcohol consumption, diabetes, and first symptoms emerged as significantly associated with overall and salivary gland toxicity. In addition, dose-volume parameters of the buccal mucosa, pharyngeal constrictor, and tongue correlated with acute mucositis, dysphagia, and xerostomia. Radiomic analysis revealed that larger and flatter target volumes were linked to increased toxicities, with PTV (Planning Target Volume) size strongly associated with hematological effects. The LKB model further identified parameters characterising the dose-response relationship for xerostomia, dysphagia, acute gastrointestinal toxicity, and overall acute toxicity. Conclusion The study identified significant factors influencing post-treatment health status and established LKB model parameters associated with radiation-induced complications.

title: Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence in Pre-Implant Radiographic Imaging: A Structured Qualitative Synthesis of Performance Across Imaging Modalities and AI Architectures.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate contemporary evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) applied to radiographic imaging for pre-implant dental assessment and treatment planning, with emphasis on the distinction between technical algorithmic performance and clinically oriented planning outcomes. Materials and methods Peer-reviewed original studies published from January 2021 through December 2025 were identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, and supplementary searches. Eligible studies used radiographic imaging as an integral input to AI for pre-implant assessment, planning, decision support, virtual positioning, or outcome prediction. Reporting completeness was assessed with CLAIM 2024. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-3 for eligible diagnostic/test-accuracy studies, PROBAST+AI for the prognostic prediction-model study, and RoB 2 for the randomized clinical study. Owing to heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively. Results Thirty-six studies were included. CBCT was the predominant modality. Applications included anatomical detection and segmentation, bone assessment, decision support, implant-position prediction, automated virtual placement, workflow integration, and preoperative outcome prediction. Segmentation and anatomical-analysis studies generally reported high task-specific performance, while clinically oriented positional accuracy and planning outcomes were more variable. AI frequently reduced workflow time. QUADAS-3 was applicable to five studies; four had high overall risk of bias and one unclear risk. The prognostic prediction-model and randomized clinical studies also had high risk of bias under their respective tools. Conclusions AI shows greatest current support for anatomical analysis and selected workflow tasks. Evidence for autonomous implant positioning and outcome prediction remains limited and heterogeneous. Current findings support clinician-supervised integration, with further multicenter external testing, standardized clinically meaningful outcomes, reproducibility, and prospective evaluation required before broader routine implementation.

title: Rapid noncontrast MRI screening for iliac and left renal vein compression: A practical bSSFP technique.
abstract: ObjectivesTo describe a rapid, widely available, noncontrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for first-line morphologic assessment of suspected iliac and left renal vein compression in patients with symptoms potentially related to pelvic venous disorders.MethodsWe use a two-stack axial two-dimensional balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) acquisition extending from the renal hila through the iliac bifurcation. The sequence is available on major MRI platforms as TrueFISP (Siemens), FIESTA (GE), or bTFE (Philips). Typical 1.5-T parameters are TR/TE 3.0-3.8/1.5-1.9 ms, flip angle 60-80°, 5-mm slice thickness, and 1.3-1.6-mm in-plane resolution. Localized shimming is performed for each stack.ResultsThe abbreviated examination requires approximately 10 minutes of scanner time, including planning and breath-hold acquisitions. It depicts the site and degree of iliac or left renal vein compression and demonstrates collateral pathways that may support physiologic relevance. Morphologic abnormalities are interpreted in the clinical context and are not considered diagnostic of a symptomatic syndrome in isolation.ConclusionsA short bSSFP protocol can provide a practical, radiation-free gateway examination when comprehensive MR venography is unavailable or undesirable. It may facilitate appropriate referral and procedural planning, while invasive assessment, including intravascular ultrasound when stenting is contemplated, remains necessary in selected patients.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R 2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: A Study on Renal Artery Variations by CT Angiography and Their Clinical Importance.
abstract: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, anatomical variations, and branching patterns of the renal arteries using multiphasic computed tomography angiography (CTA), based on the modified classification proposed by Cases et al (2017). Understanding renal artery variations is essential for preoperative planning, renal transplantation, endovascular procedures, and urological interventions.Materials and MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 1220 abdominal CTA studies performed between March 2020 and June 2024. Fourteen cases were excluded according to predetermined exclusion criteria, resulting in 1206 studies being included in the final analysis (700 males, 520 females). All examinations were performed using a 128-slice CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM; syngo CT VC 40). CTA protocols included 5-mm acquisition and 1-mm reconstruction, with administration of 100-120 mL of iodinated contrast at 5-6 mL/s via an 18G antecubital cannula. Post-processing involved multiplanar reformation, volume rendering, and 3D reconstruction. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed all studies. Renal arteries were categorized into Types A-E and Patterns I-V. "Early division" (Types B and E) and "polar branches" (Types C and D) were further grouped for analytical purposes.ResultsAmong 1206 CTA studies, Type A (normal hilar artery) was the most common in both kidneys, with a slightly higher prevalence on the right (74.29%) than on the left (67.99%). Polar branches were more frequent in the left kidney, whereas early divisions were more common in the right kidney. Pattern 1 was predominant bilaterally (RK: 85.73%; LK: 77.61%), followed by Pattern 2. Significant differences were observed between the kidneys in the distribution of Types A, C, D, and Patterns 1 and 2.ConclusionCTA provides excellent visualization of renal artery variations, enabling precise classification and improving surgical, interventional, and transplant planning. Recognition of these anatomical differences is essential for minimizing procedural complications.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
abstract: Background Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients. Methods A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole. Results Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease. Conclusion Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection.
abstract: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.

title: Swin-WaveNet: frequency-guided boundary restoration for robust skin lesion segmentation.
abstract: Accurate skin lesion segmentation remains difficult when dermoscopic boundaries are fragmented by hair occlusion, uneven illumination, or weak local contrast. To address this problem, the authors propose Swin-WaveNet, a frequency-guided encoder-decoder that combines a Swin Transformer backbone with wavelet decomposition and selective state-space modeling. Rather than passing skip features directly to the decoder, the proposed method separates low-frequency semantic information from high-frequency details, selectively refines boundary-related responses, and suppresses artifact-induced activation prior to feature reconstruction. The main results are reported as the mean and standard deviation of the sample over three runs. title: Late-onset hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction in a childhood cancer survivor treated with cranial irradiation.
abstract: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction is a well-recognized late complication in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) treated with cranial irradiation. We report a 42-year-old male with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at 5 years of age and treated with chemotherapy and 26 Gray whole-brain irradiation. He presented with right upper extremity paresis due to bilateral chronic subdural hematomas. Following burr-hole drainage for the left chronic subdural hematoma, he developed anorexia, fatigue, and hyponatremia and was referred to the endocrinology department. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated hypothalamic adrenal insufficiency, severe adult growth hormone deficiency, mild gonadal dysfunction, and mixed hypothyroidism. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a suprasellar arachnoid cyst with compression of the pituitary gland. To our knowledge, this represents one of the longest reported intervals between childhood cancer treatment and the diagnosis of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, which became clinically apparent 37 years after treatment following a prolonged asymptomatic period. This case suggests that hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction may remain clinically silent and gradually progress for decades before becoming unmasked by the physiological stress, highlighting the need for prolonged, potentially lifelong, endocrine surveillance in CCS.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Combined With Biopsy for the Preoperative Diagnosis of a Rare Pelvic Schwannoma: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Primary pelvic schwannomas are rare and often misdiagnosed due to non-specific imaging features. Accurate preoperative evaluation remains a challenge. The clinical utility of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis and targeted biopsy was evaluated for the preoperative diagnosis and management of a pelvic schwannoma. CASE REPORT A 66-year-old man presented with dysuria and lumbago. Imaging revealed a large, mixed cystic-solid pelvic mass. Conventional ultrasound demonstrated a predominantly cystic-solid lesion with limited Doppler flow, whereas CEUS showed progressive dendritic enhancement of the viable solid component from the periphery toward the center, with non-enhancement of cystic or necrotic areas. TIC analysis demonstrated a distinctive "equal-in and slow-out" perfusion pattern, supported by quantitative parameters (rise time, time to peak, fall time, and washout area under the curve). Based on these perfusion characteristics, ultrasound-guided biopsy was directed toward hyperenhanced viable regions while avoiding necrotic zones, thereby improving tissue sampling accuracy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed S-100 and SOX-10 positivity, establishing a definitive diagnosis. Complete surgical resection with bladder defect repair was performed. Postoperatively, urinary function recovered, and no recurrent urinary or pelvic symptoms were reported during outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Quantitative CEUS-TIC analysis combined with targeted biopsy provides an effective preoperative diagnostic strategy for pelvic schwannomas. The observed CEUS-TIC perfusion pattern may correspond to the heterogeneous microvascular distribution of Antoni A and Antoni B regions; however, this hypothesis requires validation in future imaging-pathology correlation studies.

title: Seven Novel Sonographic Signs
abstract: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency and the Gentle Wave Sign for the tardus-parvus waveform are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these seven signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Core Muscle Injury: A Combined Orthopaedic and General Surgery Algorithmic Approach for Diagnosis, Imaging, and Treatment.
abstract: » Core muscle injury (CMI) is a common cause of groin pain in athletes and reflects pathology of the inguinal canal, rectus abdominis-adductor longus (RA-AL) aponeurosis, and pubic symphysis. » There is a substantial lack of consensus on terminology and diagnostic criteria for CMI, hindering standardized evaluation, management, and research initiatives. » Diagnosis relies on structured history, physical examinations, and provocative maneuvers to identify CMI and concurrent pathology, and fluid-sensitive pelvic magnetic resonance imaging to characterize RA-AL injury. » Treatment strategies differ across sports medicine physicians, general surgeons, and orthopaedic surgeons, underscoring the need for early cross-departmental referrals to ensure all contributing pathologies are comprehensively identified and addressed. » When both adductor/RA-AL aponeurosis and inguinal canal/abdominal wall pathologies are present, prioritizing collaborative cases between orthopaedic and general surgeons is essential for decreasing operating room time, streamlining rehabilitation, and optimizing return-to-sport outcomes.

title: Enhancing Structural Quality in Medical X-ray Super-Resolution via Domain-Aware Loss
abstract: Abstract Upscaling medical X-ray images is more challenging than enhancing natural images, because preserving accurate structural and boundary information is more important for diagnostic correctness than producing a realistic appearance. Super-resolution methods such as SRGAN, ESRGAN, and the Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) perform well on natural images, but when applied to medical images they can cause texture hallucination, obscure anatomical boundaries, and remove clinically important features. This study presents a comprehensive comparison of four approaches: standard SRGAN, standard ESRGAN with VGG-based perceptual loss, HAT with L1 loss, and the proposed optimised models ESRGAN_USELoss and HAT_USELoss, which incorporate a domain-specific loss function designed for X-ray imaging. The proposed USELoss (U-Net, Sobel and Edge Loss) replaces the computationally heavy VGG19 perceptual loss with a lightweight U-Net encoder that preserves multi-scale anatomical structures, and adds a Sobel-based edge loss to improve boundary accuracy, prioritising diagnostic fidelity over perceptual sharpness. On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

title: Oral Foregut Duplicate cyst presenting as tongue-tie in a pediatric patient: a clinicopathologic case report
abstract: Abstract Oral foregut duplication cysts (OFDCs) are rare congenital anomalies arising from abnormal foregut development during embryogenesis, characterized by ectopic gastrointestinal or respiratory epithelium within the oral cavity. We present the case of a 6-year-old boy referred to with a presumptive diagnosis of ankyloglossia ("tongue-tie") who was found to have a well-circumscribed midline cystic mass within the intrinsic muscles of the tongue. MRI demonstrated a homogeneous T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense lesion with increased diffusivity and minimal wall enhancement. The mass was excised via a ventral tongue approach and delivered intact. Histopathologic examination revealed a cyst wall lined by ciliated respiratory-type epithelium with an underlying smooth muscular layer, consistent with an oral foregut duplication cyst. The differential diagnosis, including ranula, leiomyoma, rhabdomyoma, and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, is discussed. This case highlights the importance of considering foregut duplication cysts in the differential diagnosis of congenital tongue masses, particularly when clinical presentation mimics ankyloglossia. Complete surgical excision is curative, with a low risk of recurrence.

title: Reproducibility-Aware Evaluation of Hierarchical Multiple- Instance Learning for Patient-Level Thrombosis Detection from Compression Ultrasound
abstract: Abstract Background To provide a reproducibility-aware evaluation of multi-site cine multiple-instance learning (MS-CineMIL) versus a fixed 8-frame imaging baseline under patient-level five-fold cross-validation, and to examine whether the nominal ROC AUC difference reproduces after field completion and runtime environment control. The study delineates aggregation applicability boundaries rather than presupposing a stable advantage. Methods The public ThrombUS+ Dataset #1 Training Set (v1.0; 594 subjects, 2,341 DICOM cine clips) was used. Thrombosis is a per-site label, so the patient-level endpoint was defined as engineering-positive: raw Thrombosis = 1 for any record of the same SubjectID (81/594). After quality control, 2,327 cines were retained. Partitions used SubjectID isolation. Primary metric: ROC AUC; secondary: PR AUC, Brier score. Model differences were tested by 10,000-resample patient-level paired bootstrap (empirical two-sided P values; Bonferroni α = 0.0167). Results In the V1 historical frozen analysis, the ROC AUC difference of MS-CineMIL versus the fixed 8-frame baseline was + 0.0740 (95% CI 0.0043 to 0.1454, P = 0.039), failing Bonferroni correction. In the same-environment controlled comparison, the difference was − 0.0283 (95% CI − 0.1177 to 0.0608, P = 0.538) with a larger Brier error (+ 0.0374, P < 0.001). The baseline re-run yielded 0.6390; the complete model ROC AUC was 0.6419. The between-run baseline shift (0.0711) matched the nominal gain (+ 0.0740); no stable advantage emerged. Conclusions The V1 frozen difference did not pass multiple-comparison correction, was not reproduced under controlled comparison, and was accompanied by a larger Brier error. Evidence supports boundary auditing of model components, field completeness, and aggregation strategies, but not stable superiority, clinical deployment, external applicability, or novelty claims.

title: Adenosquamous carcinoma of the colon with an aberrant MLH1 immunostaining pattern: a diagnostic pitfall in mismatch repair assessment
abstract: Abstract Background Adenosquamous carcinoma (ASC) is a rare histological subtype of colorectal cancer (CRC) that carries a poor prognosis and has been associated with a distinct molecular profile - higher frequency of mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR), PD-L1 overexpression, and KRAS mutations. With recent advances in CRC therapeutics, molecular characterization of rare histological subtypes has become increasingly important. Here, we report a case of colorectal ASC with a distinctive dMMR immunohistochemical profile and provide a review of the literature on this rare colorectal neoplasm. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 64-year-old woman who presented with a three-month history of worsening abdominal pain and recent-onset hematochezia. Abdominal CT revealed a large mass involving the right colon. She underwent a total pelvic exenteration. Histopathology showed a high-grade, poorly differentiated tumor with mixed glandular and squamous components, staged as pT4b pN1a. Immunohistochemistry confirmed both glandular and squamous differentiation. Mismatch repair protein analysis showed loss of PMS2 expression and a granular, dot-like MLH1 staining pattern—interpreted as loss of expression and consistent with a known clone-specific artifact—while MSH2 and MSH6 were retained, supporting a dMMR phenotype. The patient received mFLOX chemotherapy but died four months postoperatively due to disease-related complications. Discussion This case illustrates the classic clinicopathological features of ASC, alongside a dMMR immunoprofile that may carry therapeutic relevance given the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in MSI-high colorectal tumors. The findings also underscore the importance of correctly recognizing clone-specific MLH1 staining artifacts, as misinterpretation could falsely suggest isolated PMS2 loss and trigger unnecessary germline testing for Lynch syndrome. Given the rarity of ASC and its limited molecular characterization, accurate MMR status assessment remains critical for guiding treatment decisions and avoiding diagnostic pitfalls.

title: Contour-free multi-instance learning versus conventional CT features for preoperative Ki-67 stratification in gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors: a retrospective comparison
abstract: Abstract Background : Manual tumor contouring adds a separate preprocessing step to CT-based prediction. We therefore evaluated whether complete-series multiinstance learning (MIL) could perform preoperative Ki-67 stratification from dual-phase CT without tumor contours and provide greater discrimination than conventional CT features. Methods : This retrospective study included 61 patients. Ki-67 cutoffs of 5%, 8%, and 10% defined three cutoff-specific tasks. Patients whose reported Ki-67 interval spanned a cutoff were excluded only from the corresponding task. Twenty-one conventional variables were analyzed with two conventional models, and frozen ResNet-18 features from the complete arterial and venous phase series were analyzed separately with five MIL methods. Four prespecified equal-logit fusion combinations were evaluated. Patient-level stratified fivefold cross-validation was repeated 10 times. title: Correlation between Serum MMP-1/TIMP-1 Ratio and the Severity of Diabetic Retinopathy in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of blindness among the working-age population. Current screening and grading primarily rely on fundus imaging, lacking serological markers that reflect early molecular pathological changes. There is an urgent need to identify biomarkers for early warning and progression assessment of DR. Purpose To investigate the correlation between serum levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, TIMP-1, and their ratios with the severity of DR in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), providing serological references for early identification and risk assessment of DR progression. Methods and Results Sixty-four T2DM patients were enrolled and divided into three groups based on fundus findings: Non DR group (n = 31), non-proliferative DR (NPDR) group (n = 17), and proliferative DR (PDR) group (n = 16). Serum levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, and TIMP-1 were measured using ELISA, and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 and MMP-2/TIMP-1 ratios were calculated. Results showed that serum MMP-1 levels and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio exhibited an increasing trend across the three groups and were significantly positively correlated with DR severity grading (r = 0.283, P = 0.023; r = 0.344, P = 0.005). No statistically significant differences were observed in MMP-2, TIMP-1 levels, or the MMP-2/TIMP-1 ratio among the groups, nor were they significantly correlated with DR severity. Conclusion Serum MMP-1 levels and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio increase with the severity of DR and may serve as novel serological candidate markers for reflecting DR progression. The MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio showed a stronger correlation than the single marker, suggesting its potential value as a comprehensive indicator of extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and remodeling balance in assessing DR progression. Future studies with larger sample sizes and combined ocular local samples are needed for further validation.

title: Interpretable Concept-Bottleneck Vision-Language Model Predicts Pathologic Complete Response From Longitudinal Breast DCE-MRI
abstract: Abstract Deep learning can predict neoadjuvant treatment response in breast cancer, but most models are black boxes whose reasoning clinicians cannot verify, limiting adoption. We developed an interpretable concept-bottleneck vision-language model (CB-VLM) that predicts pathologic complete response (pCR) from pre-treatment and early-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI, routing every prediction through eleven radiologist-recognizable, BI-RADS-style imaging concepts plus age and molecular subtype. Trained on 753 patients from the multicenter I-SPY2 trial, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.76 on encoder-held-out data (n = 144) and generalized to an independent I-SPY1 cohort (AUC 0.71; n = 110). Accuracy rose with model confidence (88% versus 58% on borderline predictions), and early change in functional tumor volume was the dominant predictor across both cohorts. To our knowledge, this is the first large vision-language model to generate concept-grounded reasoning for breast DCE-MRI treatment response prediction, reframing a black-box task as transparent, auditable, and generalizable.

title: Thenar Muscle Thickness Assessed by Point-of-Care Ultrasound and Geriatric Vulnerability in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Malnutrition and sarcopenia frequently coexist in hospitalized older adults. Thenar muscle thickness (TMT) may provide a pragmatic correlate of geriatric vulnerability, but its clinical relevance is unestablished. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, cross-sectional pilot study analyzed 50 hospitalized patients aged 75 years or older, admitted between October and December 2024. Unadjusted Spearman correlations assessed associations between TMT and Mini Nutritional Assessment–Short Form (MNA-SF), Braden, and Conley scores. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were calculated for these three correlations. Results Mean age was 86.2 years; 60.0% of participants were women. Mean TMT was 2.62 cm (SD, 0.48). Overall, 84.0% of patients were malnourished or at risk of malnutrition, 66.0% had high pressure-injury risk, and 90.0% had a Conley score indicating fall risk. Higher TMT correlated with higher MNA-SF (rho = 0.760; 95% CI, 0.595–0.859; P < 0.001) and Braden scores (rho = 0.560; 95% CI, 0.340–0.729; P < 0.001), and with lower Conley scores (Rho = − 0.406; 95% CI, − 0.627 to − 0.141; P = 0.003). Associations remained directionally consistent after adjustment for age and sex: partial rho was 0.753 (95% CI, 0.572–0.865) for MNA-SF, 0.510 (95% CI, 0.251–0.709) for Braden, and − 0.361 (95% CI, − 0.602 to − 0.054) for Conley. TMT was not significantly associated with length of stay (Rho = − 0.240; P = 0.093). Conclusions In very old hospitalized adults, lower TMT was associated with poorer nutritional status and greater fall and pressure-injury risk. TMT may complement multidimensional geriatric assessment, but the small, unadjusted pilot design and absence of a sarcopenia reference standard preclude diagnostic or independent prognostic claims.

title: Evaluating the Osteogenic potential of S. officinale against Glucocorticoid-induced Osteoporosis using in vivo model
abstract: Abstract Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is characterized by impaired bone formation, increased bone resorption and disruption of bone mineralization. The present study investigated the osteoprotective potential of Symphytum officinale ( S. officinale ) aqueous root extract using a dexamethasone-induced osteoporosis model in adult zebrafish ( Danio rerio ). Phytochemical screening and LC–MS analysis were performed to characterize the extract, followed by developmental toxicity assessment. Adult zebrafish were divided into control, dexamethasone-treated and low- and high-dose S. officinale -treated groups. Bone regeneration and mineralization were evaluated using histopathology, Alizarin Red staining, scale morphometry and ICP-MS analysis of calcium and phosphorus. Hydroxyproline, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) assays were performed to assess collagen content and bone remodelling. The extract showed the presence of alkaloids, terpenoids, phytosterols and other bioactive constituents, including quercetin derivatives and biochanin A, while no developmental toxicity was observed at the tested concentrations. Dexamethasone induced marked alterations in tissue architecture, reduced mineral deposition and scale size and disrupted calcium and phosphorus levels. S. officinale treatment improved skeletal morphology, mineralization, scale size and mineral content, with pronounced effects on several parameters at the higher dose. The extract also modulated hydroxyproline, ALP and TRAP activities, indicating concentration-dependent effects on bone remodelling. Hence, S. officinale demonstrates osteoprotective potential against dexamethasone-induced skeletal alterations in zebrafish.

title: When tiny lungs Struggle to breathe; a rare cause of Refractory Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
abstract: Abstract Alveolar capillary dysplasia with malpositioned pulmonary veins (ACD/MPV) is a lethal congenital lung disorder with a mortality rate of almost 100%. Infants deteriorate within the first 24 hours of life. Here, we present a 2-day old female child born of full term normal vaginal delivery and cried immediately after birth. The baby presented with Respiratory distress within 6 hours of life and was put on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 2-D echo revealed no congenital heart disease. The child continued to have pulmonary hypertension non-responsive to pharmacotherapy and eventually passed away. A post mortem histopathology examination revealed immature lung parenchyma with arrest in the saccular phase, thickened alveolar septae with abnormally positioned pulmonary capillaries. Focally, there were thin-walled vessels invested in the same adventitial sheath as the pulmonary arteries. The pulmonary arterioles exhibited features of pulmonary artery hypertension. Based on this constellation of features, the baby was diagnosed with ACD/MPV. The rarity and the focal nature of this condition make it a diagnostic challenge in terms of awareness of this entity and subsequent interpretation. Conclusion : This case reiterates the importance of knowing and understanding normal histology. A high degree of clinical suspicion as well as expertise in the field of thoracic pathology is required for appropriate diagnosis.

title: Possible Neurosarcoidosis Presenting with Chronic Pachymeningeal Disease, Extensive Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis, and Recurrent Seizures: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Neurosarcoidosis is an uncommon manifestation of sarcoidosis that can involve the meninges, cranial nerves, brain parenchyma, spinal cord, and cerebral vasculature. Its clinical and radiological manifestations frequently overlap with infectious, inflammatory, neoplastic, and vascular disorders, creating substantial diagnostic challenges. Case presentation: A 42-year-old woman presented with recurrent abnormal involuntary movements and progressive neurological deterioration. Her illness had evolved over approximately 12 years, beginning with chronic headache followed by right periorbital discomfort, progressive visual impairment, facial sensory symptoms, and later progressive focal neurological deficits. She was initially evaluated for a brain tumor and subsequently received prolonged anti-tuberculous therapy on more than one occasion for presumed tuberculous meningitis, with incomplete or absent clinical response. Over the months preceding the current admission, she developed progressive hemiparesis, abnormal posturing, facial twitching, dysarthria, urinary symptoms, and recurrent focal seizures that subsequently became prolonged and generalized with impaired consciousness. Serial brain imaging reported chronic pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement, cortical and subcortical abnormalities, features of raised intracranial pressure, and progressive vascular complications. Contrast-enhanced CT subsequently demonstrated superior sagittal sinus and bilateral cavernous sinus thrombosis with multifocal cerebral venous infarction/edema and small bilateral hemispheric and tentorial/interhemispheric subdural hematomas. Laboratory evaluation did not demonstrate a clear alternative infectious or systemic autoimmune etiology. A skin punch biopsy of healed chest lesions showed a sclerosing/keloidal scar without histological evidence of sarcoidosis or tuberculosis. Abdominopelvic ultrasonography additionally demonstrated chronic portal vein occlusion/thrombosis with periportal collateral vessels and periportal fibrosis. In the context of the prolonged clinical course, longitudinal meningeal imaging abnormalities, exclusion of several important mimickers, and multidisciplinary reassessment, a working diagnosis of possible neurosarcoidosis was made. Anti-tuberculous therapy was discontinued. The patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids followed by oral prednisone and early steroid-sparing methotrexate with folic acid. At four-month follow-up, she demonstrated substantial clinical improvement, including recovery of baseline mentation, resolution of severe headache, cessation of clinical seizures, improvement in motor weakness and abnormal movements, and improvement/stabilization of visual and functional symptoms. Conclusion: This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of chronic meningeal inflammatory disease presenting with progressive neurological dysfunction and extensive cerebral venous thrombosis. Persistent pachymeningeal abnormalities, failure to respond to prolonged anti-tuberculous treatment, and progressive neurological manifestations should prompt reconsideration of alternative inflammatory diagnoses. The coexistence of cerebral and chronic portal venous thrombosis raises the possibility of a systemic inflammatory or prothrombotic contribution, although a direct causal relationship with sarcoidosis could not be established. Clinical improvement following corticosteroid-based immunosuppression with methotrexate supports the working diagnosis, but the absence of tissue confirmation remains an important limitation.

title: Umbilical Cord Hernia is Not an Isolated Pathology: High Rate of Associated Anomalies in a Tertiary Center Cohort
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile of umbilical cord hernia (UCH), a defect often considered a minor variant of omphalocele, with a specific focus on the prevalence and spectrum of associated congenital anomalies. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 45 neonates with anterior abdominal wall defects treated between August 2019 and July 2024. Patients were categorized into three groups: omphalocele (n = 15), gastroschisis (n = 19), and UCH (n = 11). Demographic data, prenatal diagnosis, associated anomalies, surgical management, and outcomes were analyzed. Results In the UCH group, six patients (54.5%) had at least one major associated anomaly. Major cardiac anomalies were present in 45.5% (5/11), chromosomal anomalies in 27.3% (3/11), and genitourinary anomalies in 36.4% (4/11) of patients. The spectrum included Tetralogy of Fallot, Trisomy 13, 18, 21, and genetic syndromes (e.g., 3MC syndrome). Four patients (36.4%) had isolated UCH. Mortality in the UCH group was 18.2%, exclusively occurring in patients with major associated anomalies. Conclusion Contrary to traditional belief, umbilical cord hernia is frequently associated with serious cardiac, chromosomal, and multisystemic anomalies. These findings necessitate a paradigm shift in management, advocating for comprehensive screening including echocardiography, renal ultrasound, and genetic evaluation in all neonates with UCH, similar to the standard for omphalocele.

title: Implementation of novel approaches for management and treatment of brain tumours
abstract: Primary brain tumours remain among the most difficult cancers to treat because of their molecular heterogeneity, infiltrative growth and the blood–brain barrier (BBB), which restricts drug delivery. For almost two decades, management of glioblastoma, the most common malignant primary brain tumour in adults, has rested on maximal safe resection followed by radiotherapy with temozolomide. Recent years have brought a more differentiated picture. Integrated molecular classification (WHO CNS5) and DNA methylation profiling have sharpened diagnosis; fluorescence-guided surgery and tumour treating fields have extended the established armamentarium; the IDH inhibitor vorasidenib (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.39; 95% CI 0.27–0.56 versus placebo) and BRAF/MEK inhibition with dabrafenib plus trametinib have delivered the first clearly biomarker-directed successes in adult and paediatric glioma respectively; and immunotherapy, including checkpoint blockade, dendritic cell vaccination and intraventricular CAR T cells, is under active investigation with mixed results. Regulatory approvals of vorasidenib (2024) and dordaviprone (2025) have since extended the biomarker-directed options, and ultrasound-mediated BBB opening illustrates a delivery-focused strategy. In parallel, machine-learning tools now support tumour classification, segmentation and response assessment, and are well placed to inform patient selection, end-point definition and trial design. This review summarises the clinical evidence for each approach, highlights pharmacological issues (CNS penetration, response end-points, safety and exposure–response relationships) and discusses barriers to implementation, including trial design, external validation of AI tools and equitable access.

title: Spinal intradural arachnoid cyst in an infant with motor developmental delay showing intraoperative MEP improvement: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Spinal intradural arachnoid cysts (SIACs) are relatively rare, but they can cause neurological symptoms. The authors report a case of an infant with an SIAC presenting with motor developmental delay, highlighting the intraoperative improvement of motor evoked potentials (MEPs). Observations A 14-month-old girl presented with a lower limb motor developmental delay. Spinal MRI revealed an SIAC at the C7-T4 level, compressing the spinal cord from the dorsal side. She underwent surgical fenestration of the cyst. Intraoperatively, transcranial MEP amplitudes in the lower extremities were initially lower than those in the upper extremities. Following cyst fenestration and decompression, the MEP amplitudes increased more than 10-fold compared to the baseline and were maintained. Postoperatively, her motor functions gradually improved. By 5 months after surgery, her developmental delay had resolved, and she achieved age-appropriate motor milestones. Lessons In this pediatric case of an SIAC, surgical decompression led to a significant and immediate increase in MEP amplitudes. This physiological change was followed by an improvement in the patient's motor development, suggesting that intraoperative MEP monitoring can be a useful tool for evaluating the immediate effect of decompression in infants with an SIAC. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26285.

She underwent surgical fenestration of the cyst. Intraoperatively, transcranial MEP amplitudes in the lower extremities were initially lower than those in the upper extremities. Following cyst fenestration and decompression, the MEP amplitudes increased more than 10-fold compared to the baseline and were maintained. Postoperatively, her motor functions gradually improved. By 5 months after surgery, her developmental delay had resolved, and she achieved age-appropriate motor milestones.

In this pediatric case of an SIAC, surgical decompression led to a significant and immediate increase in MEP amplitudes. title: Skull infarction and chronic subdural exudates in a pediatric patient with sickle cell anemia: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Skull infarction is a rare sickle cell disease (SCD) complication. While epidural hematomas from calvarial infarction have been sporadically reported, subdural collections and sterile exudates mimicking intracranial empyema remain poorly characterized. Observations A 6-year-old boy with nonverbal autism and SCD presented with progressive periorbital swelling, fever, and extremity pain. CT raised concern for orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, and subdural empyema. MRI revealed a diffuse heterogeneous calvarial marrow signal with multifocal nonenhancement and restricted diffusion consistent with bone infarction, alongside right convexity subdural fluid and bilateral epidural and subperiosteal rim-enhancing collections demonstrating susceptibility artifacts. Emergency craniotomy and orbital exploration yielded hemosiderin-stained fluid, and necrotic bone without purulence. All operative cultures were negative. Postoperative imaging demonstrated expansion of the subdural collection to 8 mm with 6-7 mm of midline shift, managed with dexamethasone. Nine months later, the patient re-presented with recurrent subperiosteal hemorrhage without infection. Lessons Calvarial infarction in SCD can produce sterile collections that mimic infectious processes. Intraoperative findings and culture data are essential in distinguishing these entities. Middle meningeal artery embolization warrants caution in SCD patients, given the risk of moyamoya vasculopathy. This case underscores the importance of a broad differential when evaluating SCD patients with periorbital swelling and intracranial collections. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26291.

title: Quantitative, longitudinal measurements of response to immunotherapy for glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI in a long-term survivor treated with autologous tumor lysate-loaded dendritic cell vaccine: an illustrative case.
abstract: Background Neurosurgeons are in the forefront of developing clinical trials that harness the immune system to combat glioblastoma. Autologous tumor lysate-loaded dendritic cell vaccine (DCVax-L) is a novel immunotherapy for glioblastoma. An unmet need is to develop a sensitive, specific, feasible, clinically relevant, neuroimaging biomarker that accurately reflects response to immunotherapy. Observations This illustrative case involves a 63-year-old female who survived for 64 months following near-total resection of a glioblastoma and enrollment in a clinical trial (NCT00045968) using DCVax-L. A multivariate logistic regression model was used to assess treatment response longitudinally at 11 time points measuring predictive probability (PP) of tumor progression based on diffusion tensor imaging- and perfusion-weighted imaging-derived parameters within the contrast-enhancing region. Lesions were considered true progression (TP) if the PP was ≥ 50% and pseudoprogression (PsP; predominant treatment effects) if the PP was < 50 %. These findings were subsequently validated by histopathological analysis during resection for tumor recurrence. Lessons These findings support the use of multiparametric MRI to monitor the effects of immunotherapy in patients with glioblastoma. Such multiparametric prediction models using noninvasive, advanced neuroimaging may be helpful to differentiate TP from PsP in longitudinal assessment of treatment response. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26655.

title: Spinal subependymoma mimicking an intradural extramedullary tumor: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Spinal subependymomas are rare, benign tumors that typically arise within the spinal cord and usually appear as intramedullary lesions on MRI. The authors report a rare case of cervical spinal subependymoma with exophytic growth that mimicked an intradural extramedullary tumor on MRI. Observations A 53-year-old man presented with right-sided paresthesia. MRI revealed a spinal tumor causing marked spinal cord compression. The lesion was isointense on T1-weighted images, slightly hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed no gadolinium enhancement. A focal CSF cleft between the tumor and spinal cord led to a preoperative diagnosis of an intradural extramedullary tumor, and schwannoma was suspected. However, intraoperative pathological examination suggested a low-grade glioma, prompting a change in the surgical strategy. Subtotal resection was therefore performed to preserve neurological function. Histological examination subsequently confirmed the diagnosis of subependymoma. Lessons Spinal subependymoma may rarely present with an apparent intradural extramedullary appearance on MRI. The presence of a CSF cleft and exophytic growth should not exclude an intramedullary origin. Awareness of this atypical presentation and avoidance of anchoring bias are essential for appropriate intraoperative decision-making. When subependymoma is suspected, maximal safe resection should be prioritized over aggressive tumor removal to preserve neurological function. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26728.

title: The importance of CSF distribution for target values and risk profiling for idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus shunt surgery.
abstract: Background and purpose Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus is characterized by gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. Symptom improvement can be achieved by shunt surgery, especially regarding gait difficulties. This study investigated whether CSF volumetry can define postoperative target values associated with clinical improvement and, secondly, predict potential non-response or overdrainage complications. Materials and methods Forty-seven patients with iNPH were prospectively followed for three years after shunt surgery. Quantitative MRI was performed at baseline and at 3, 12, and 36 months postoperatively. Automatic segmentation yielded ventricular volume, subarachnoid CSF volume, ratio of ventricular and total CSF volume and ratio of total brain volume and intracranial volume. Clinical outcome was assessed using the Hellström iNPH scale. Patients were classified as responders and non-responders and further subdivided with and without overdrainage complications. Results Eighty-seven percent of patients were classified as responders. Responders demonstrated a 26% reduction in ventricular volume(139 ml at baseline and 102 ml at three years) accompanied by a >60% improvement in iNPH score. The ventricular/total CSF ratio decreased from 0.34 to 0.25. Non-responders exhibited low ratios already at baseline, due to a significantly higher subarachnoid CSF volume. Overdrainage-related postural headaches were associated withlow subarachnoid CSF volume, younger age, higher baseline iNPH score, and higher BPV/ICV ratio. Aggregate z-scores combining multiple baseline metrics improved discrimination between responders, non-responders, and patients at risk for overdrainage. Conclusions Baseline volumetry may provide target values and risk stratification for shunt surgery in iNPH. Responders showed a reduction of ventricular volume to ∼100 ml and ventricle/total CSF ratio to ∼0.25. High subarachnoid CSF volumes at baseline, however, was associated with poor response, while low subarachnoid CSF volume indicated an increased risk of postural headache. Quantitative CSF segmentation may improve patient selection and postoperative management in iNPH.

title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound: Established and Emerging Applications in Neurosciences.
abstract: Transcranial MR-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) thermoablation is an established incisionless image-guided treatment for movement disorders; however, neuroradiologist involvement in clinical decision-making and procedural workflows is highly variable and site-specific. Transcranial low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is a rapidly evolving non-invasive, image-guided technology for neuromodulation and blood-brain barrier disruption. Compared with HIFU, the optimal protocol, therapeutic mechanism, and safety limits remain uncertain for LIFU. Despite these gaps, LIFU has significant potential for neuropsychiatric and neuro-oncologic diseases. Familiarity with transcranial ultrasound principles and the pivotal role of CT and MR imaging for targeting and evaluating outcomes is increasingly important for neuroradiologists. This review uses HIFU as a clinical model to illustrate the integration of imaging into focused ultrasound workflows. We then discuss LIFU with respect to technical factors, imaging considerations, safety, and limitations. We highlight its emerging applications, including neuromodulation, targeted drug delivery, and liquid biopsy. Finally, we conclude by summarizing key knowledge gaps, outlining future directions, and proposing strategies to more actively engage neuroradiologists in this emerging field.

title: The unknown face of Sturge-Weber Syndrome type 3 - a hybrid scoping review of the literature.
abstract: Sturge-Weber syndrome (SWS) type 3 is a rare neurocutaneous disorder characterised by isolated leptomeningeal angiomatosis without facial capillary malformation or ocular involvement. Existing literature is limited to case reports and small series, resulting in incomplete characterisation of its clinical and radiological phenotype and frequent diagnostic delay. The increased prevalence of contrast-enhanced MRI has improved detection of pial angiomatosis and associated parenchymal abnormalities. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence and define current knowledge gaps. Our aim is to synthesise published data on SWS type 3, describe demographic, clinical, and imaging features, and contribute a 15-patient institutional cohort.PubMed and EMBASE were systematically searched (31 March-4 April 2025), with additional studies identified through reference screening. Eligible studies reported isolated leptomeningeal angiomatosis without port-wine birthmark and included contrast-enhanced MRI. Seventy-five published cases were identified. Heterogeneity in study design and reporting precluded quantitative pooling; data were synthesised descriptively. SWS type 3 demonstrates a consistent pattern of unilateral, predominantly occipitoparietal leptomeningeal angiomatosis, most commonly presenting with focal-onset seizures. Despite improved MRI-based recognition, substantial gaps remain regarding natural history, pathophysiology, and optimal management. Prospective, standardised studies are required to refine diagnostic criteria and guide evidence-based care.

title: Imaging-Enhanced Prediction of Upper Limb Motor Function After Stroke Using Automated Segmentation and Cluster Analysis.
abstract: Background Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, and early prediction of motor outcomes is critical for guiding individualized rehabilitation strategies. Although neuroimaging offers prognostic insights, its clinical integration remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether explainable imaging-derived features can improve the prediction of upper limb motor impairment and to identify distinct recovery profiles through cluster analysis. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 242 patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and motor function assessment. Clinical and imaging variables-including infarct volume, motor tract involvement, and subtype classification-were extracted using automated software. Predictive models for Fugl-Meyer Assessment upper extremity (FMA-UE) scores were developed using hierarchical regression, and K-means clustering was applied to standardized baseline data. Cluster characteristics were compared, and recovery profiles were visualized. Results Incorporating imaging variables improved prediction of FMA-UE scores (adjusted R²: 0.595), with motor tract lesion volume emerging as a key predictor. Cluster analysis revealed three distinct patient subgroups: Cluster 1 (mild impairments, younger age), Cluster 2 (older patients with multiple comorbidities), and Cluster 3 (severe neurological deficits, large infarcts). Functional outcomes differed significantly across clusters, with Cluster 3 showing the greatest disability (76% with follow-up modified Rankin Scale 4-6, P < 0.001). Conclusion Imaging-derived features from early magnetic resonance imaging improve the prediction of upper limb motor outcomes after stroke. Cluster-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups, supporting precision rehabilitation through personalized care planning and targeted secondary prevention.

title: Hepatic Cysts in Korea: Prevalence, Incidence, and Risk Factors Based on a 5.8-Year Follow-up Health Screening Cohort.
abstract: Background Hepatic cysts are fluid-filled liver lesions that are mostly asymptomatic, but fewer than 15% of patients present clinically significant symptoms. Reported prevalence ranges from 2.5% to 71%, yet prior studies have been limited by small populations and incomplete assessment of risk factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, incidence, and risk factors using data from a large health screening cohort in Korea. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 78,676 participants in the Health and Prevention Enhancement cohort who underwent abdominal ultrasound at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center from 2003 and 2014. Hepatic cysts were identified using a validated rule-based text-mining algorithm applied to ultrasound reports. Prevalence was estimated from baseline data. Incidence was assessed in 41,179 participants initially negative for hepatic cysts. Risk factors were determined through Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results The prevalence of hepatic cysts at baseline was 8.54% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 8.34-8.73). The incidence was 23.4 per 1,000 person-years at risk (95% CI, 22.8-24.0). Cox regression identified hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBs-Ag) positivity (hazard ratio [HR], 1.20; 95% CI, 1.00-1.45) and renal cyst presence (HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.31-1.64) as independent risk factors, whereas diabetes mellitus (HR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.54-0.77) and high physical activity (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.81-0.97) appeared protective. Conclusion This study provides the prevalence of 8.54%, incidence, and risk factors of hepatic cysts. Renal cyst presence and HBs-Ag positivity are significant risk factors, whereas high physical activity and diabetic status are protective.

title: The Current Status and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer: Clinical Applications and Research.
abstract: Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.

title: QuRad: Radiomics Feature Extraction for QuPath.
abstract: Radiomic features provide a quantitative description of tissue organization in histopathology images. QuPath, a widely used open-source platform for whole-slide image analysis, offers morphology, intensity, and Haralick texture measurements but no standardized radiomic feature set such as that of PyRadiomics. Researchers must therefore export data to external Python pipelines, interrupting their QuPath workflow. QuRad extracts radiomic features from cell detections and annotation regions directly inside QuPath. The extension and equivalent Groovy script implement 119 features: 103 two-dimensional features enabled by default and 16 optional legacy shape descriptors. We compared QuRad 0.4 with PyRadiomics 3.0.1 on identical grayscale images and pixel masks. All 103 default features met a 10 -9 absolute-or-relative agreement tolerance on a breast-cancer benchmark tile (410 cells). On 20 melanoma tiles (8,644 nuclei), 97 of 103 features met this tolerance and 6 polygon-derived shape features differed from PyRadiomics' raster-derived mesh (minimum concordance correlation coefficient 0.942). The 22 synthetic regions accepted by PyRadiomics reproduced the expected intensity and texture values. A single-threaded server benchmark reached about 1,900 nuclei per second, and processing the 184,242 cells of a whole-slide image took 2.7 min on a laptop. A random forest distinguished tumor cells from lymphocytes in melanoma (pooled macro-F1 0.853) and classified 197 tissue regions of 6 breast-cancer slides into 3 compartments (0.696). QuRad exports the features with object coordinates and extraction settings for use in QuPath or downstream analyses.

title: Impact of Triple Assessment on Surgical Decision-making in Thyroid Nodule Management.
abstract: Introduction Accurate preoperative assessment of thyroid nodules is crucial for distinguishing malignant from benign lesions and making optimal decisions. Triple assessment using clinical examination, ultrasonography (USG), and fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) has been increasingly used to improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy of triple assessment in the detection and treatment of thyroid nodules by correlating ultrasonographic findings, clinical evaluation, and FNAC results with histopathological diagnosis. Methods This study was a prospective observational study of 56 patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgical management. Data were collected prospectively using structured case record forms. Baseline information, physical examination findings, USG features, FNAC records, operative details, and histopathological reports were documented. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Frequency and percentage were used to present categorical variables. The diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination, USG, FNAC, and triple assessment was evaluated by estimating specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value, and diagnostic accuracy. Results A higher proportion of participants were female (85.7%) and were in the 41-60 years old age group. Histopathology confirmed benign lesions in 57.14% and malignant lesions in 42.86% of cases. Triple assessment achieved the most effective diagnostic accuracy, showing a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 87.50%, with a NPV of 100% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 97.86%. Conclusion Triple assessment is a dependable and useful modality for assessing thyroid nodules. Combined use of clinical examination, USG, and FNAC reduces false-negative results and supports appropriate clinical decision-making.

title: Evaluating the Interplay and Impact of Quality and Technical Variations on Performance of AI Models in Multi-Institutional Prostate MRI Datasets
abstract: PurposeTo evaluate whether visually assessed high-quality prostate MRI, as defined by the Prostate Imaging Quality (PI-QUAL) scoring system, is sufficient to ensure consistent AI model performance, or whether hidden acquisition-related technical effects introduce variability that cannot be detected through visual inspection. MethodsThis retrospective study included 568 bpMRI scans from seven institutions, classified using PI-QUAL v2 into high-quality (scores 2-3) and low-quality (score 1) groups. Quantitative image quality features were extracted using MRQy from T2w and ADC sequences. Three experiments were conducted on high-quality scans: (1) unsupervised clustering to identify hidden technical batch effects; (2) V-Net models (M) for prostate capsule segmentation on T2w using single-cluster and balanced multi-cluster training strategies; and (3) VoxelMorph-based deformable registration (M2) to align ADC maps to T2w images. Performance metrics included DSC, precision, recall, volume ratio, HD95, ASSD, and TRE. Kruskal-Wallis tests assessed cross-cluster variability, Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) evaluated performance equivalence, and bootstrap resampling quantified training efficiency. ResultsClustering identified four clusters among 277 high-quality bpMRI scans. Single-cluster models showed variable performance (DSC=0.41-0.85) with significant batch effects (p<0.001), even with 140 training samples. The balanced multi-cluster model (n=60) eliminated batch effects (p=0.075), achieved equivalent performance (p<0.001), and demonstrated 2.23-fold greater training efficiency despite using 2.3-fold fewer samples. Registration performance also varied significantly across clusters (TRE=0.86-5.47 mm, p<0.001). ConclusionAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impact AI generalizability in prostate MRI, even among high-quality scans. Quantitative clustering enables detection of technical variations and supports diversity-aware training strategies that achieve equivalent performance with 2.3-fold fewer samples while eliminating batch effects. SummaryAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impair AI generalizability in prostate MRI, even among scans meeting PI-QUAL quality standards. Clustering-based diversity-aware training strategies successfully eliminated these batch effects and achieved 2.23-fold greater training efficiency compared to single-site approaches, demonstrating that strategic technical diversity outweighs dataset size for developing robust, clinically deployable AI models. Key PointsO_LIAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impair AI performance on prostate MRI, exceeding the impact of visual image quality as assessed by PI-QUAL scoring. C_LIO_LIEven the model trained on the largest single cluster exhibited significant batch effects (p<0.001). In contrast, a balanced multi-cluster model eliminated cross-cluster variability (p=0.075) while maintaining equivalent performance and requiring a smaller sample size. C_LIO_LIDiversity-aware training achieved 2.23-fold greater training efficiency (95% CI: 2.18-2.29) with 2.3-fold fewer samples, demonstrating that technical diversity outweighs data quantity for robust AI generalization. C_LI Clinical relevanceAddressing batch effects is essential for developing reliable, generalizable AI tools for prostate MRI interpretation.
